test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The length and the breadth of a rectangular cardboard are 40 cm and 35 cm, respectively. If the biggest possible square is cut out from this cardboard, what is the area of the remaining part of the cardboard?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To cut out the biggest possible square from a rectangle, its side must equal the smaller dimension (breadth).

Side of the square = 35 cm.

The remaining portion is a rectangle with length (40 − 35) = 5 cm and breadth 35 cm.

Remaining Area = 5 × 35 = 175 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 175 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of cardboard (L) = 40 cm

Breadth of cardboard (B) = 35 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

Area of square = Side × Side

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3da016dd48823ff1757cf7324b566ebd4c7ef267854f3edd4cf1d3ff692582b7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of the original cardboard = 40 × 35 = 1400 cm²

⇒ For the biggest possible square, Side (a) = Breadth = 35 cm

⇒ Area of the cut-out square = 35 × 35 = 1225 cm²

⇒ Area of the remaining part = Area of original cardboard − Area of cut-out square

⇒ Area of the remaining part = 1400 − 1225 = 175 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 175 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Maximum Square from a Rectangle

To cut the largest possible square from a rectangle, the side length of the square must be perfectly equal to the shorter side (breadth) of the given rectangle.

Area of a Rectangle

The area of a rectangle is defined as the product of its length and breadth. Formula: Area = L × B.

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The total distance around the outside boundary of a rectangle. Formula: Perimeter = 2 × (L + B).
